KESTREL VALLEY COMMUNITY COLLEGE — HARDSHIP BURSARY REGULATIONS 2026/27
(Approved by the Student Finance Committee, 2026-05-12. Applies to awards for the academic year starting 2026-09-01.)

PART A — AWARD LEVELS
A.1 The bursary is paid at one of five levels:
    Level 0 — no award
    Level 1 — EUR 500
    Level 2 — EUR 1,200
    Level 3 — EUR 2,000
    Level 4 — EUR 3,000
A.2 The level is determined by the PER-CAPITA COUNTABLE INCOME of the assessed household (Part D), using the table in Part E, subject to the asset rule in Part F.

PART B — DEPENDENCY STATUS
B.1 A student is INDEPENDENT if on the reference date (1 September of the award year) at least one of the following is true:
    (a) the student is 24 years old or older;
    (b) the student is married;
    (c) the student has at least one dependent child living with them;
    (d) the student was in local-authority care after their 16th birthday.
B.2 Otherwise the student is DEPENDENT.
B.3 For all purposes of these regulations, a registered civil partnership is treated exactly like a marriage, and a registered civil partner exactly like a spouse.
B.4 Dependency status is fixed on the reference date; later changes apply only from the next award year.

PART C — ASSESSED HOUSEHOLD
C.1 Dependent students: the assessed household is the parent(s) the student normally lives with, their spouse/partner if any, the student, and all other children living in that household.
C.2 Independent students: the assessed household is the student, their spouse (if any), and their dependent children (if any). Parents' income and household are NOT assessed for independent students, even if parental data was supplied on the form.
C.3 Household size = number of persons in the assessed household.

PART D — COUNTABLE INCOME
D.1 Countable income = sum over the assessed household (excluding children under 18) of: gross employment income for the previous calendar year (2025), net self-employment profit, pensions, and taxable benefits.
D.2 Excluded from countable income: child benefit; disability-related allowances; student loans and grants; earnings from the college's WORK-STUDY programme (for any student); one-off gifts under EUR 1,000.
D.3 Dependent students only: deduct EUR 2,000 from the household's countable income for each OTHER child of the household enrolled full-time in higher education.
D.4 Per-capita countable income = countable income ÷ household size, rounded to the nearest euro.

PART E — LEVEL TABLE (per-capita countable income, EUR)
| Per-capita countable income | Level |
|-----------------------------|-------|
| up to 7,000                 | 4     |
| 7,001 – 10,500              | 3     |
| 10,501 – 14,000             | 2     |
| 14,001 – 18,000             | 1     |
| above 18,000                | 0     |

PART F — ASSETS
F.1 If the assessed household's savings and investments (excluding the main home and one car) exceed EUR 40,000, the level is capped at Level 1.
F.2 Assets are declared on the form; the college may request statements.

PART G — PROCEDURE (reference)
G.1 Applications close 2026-10-15. Late applications are assessed only if funds remain.
G.2 Evidence: P60/annual payslip or tax assessment for each income line; certificate for civil status; enrolment certificates for siblings.
G.3 Payments are made in two instalments (November, February) to the student's own account.
G.4 Students must be enrolled at least half-time on the census date (2026-10-01).
G.5 Appeals go to the Student Finance Committee within 28 days of the decision letter.
G.6 Assessors record the dependency decision, the household composition, each countable and excluded income line, and the per-capita figure on the assessment sheet, so that the decision can be checked by a second assessor.
G.7 Amounts are taken in whole euros as declared and evidenced; the college does not index 2025 income to 2026 prices.

PART H — FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q: I filled in my parents' details because the form asked for them. Does that matter? — A: The form collects parental data from everyone. Whether it is used depends only on Part B.
Q: My partner and I are not married but have lived together for years. — A: Cohabitation without marriage or registered civil partnership does not make a student independent.
Q: My work-study job is my main income. — A: Work-study earnings are still excluded (D.2).
Q: My sibling is at university; can I deduct that? — A: Only dependent students' households get the D.3 deduction.

PART I — WORKED EXAMPLES (illustrative, fictional students)
I.1 Dependent student, age 19, lives with mother (employment 2025: EUR 31,000) and brother (17). Household 3. Countable 31,000. Per capita 10,333 → Level 3.
I.2 Dependent student, age 21, lives with both parents (employment EUR 48,000 and EUR 12,000) and a sister (22) studying full-time at university. Household 4. Countable 60,000 − 2,000 (D.3) = 58,000. Per capita 14,500 → Level 1.
I.3 Independent student, age 26, single, no children. Employment EUR 11,400; work-study EUR 2,900 (excluded). Household 1. Per capita 11,400 → Level 2.
I.4 Independent student, age 22, married, one child aged 2. Spouse employment EUR 24,600; student no income; child benefit EUR 3,000 (excluded). Household 3. Per capita 8,200 → Level 3.
I.5 Independent student, age 30, savings EUR 52,000, income EUR 6,000. Per capita 6,000 → Level 4 by table, capped to Level 1 by F.1.

PART J — RELATED FUNDS (not assessed on this form)
J.1 Childcare Support Fund: separate application; up to EUR 1,500 per year towards registered childcare.
J.2 Travel Grant: students living more than 40 km from campus may claim 50 % of a public-transport season ticket.
J.3 Emergency Loan: interest-free, up to EUR 800, repayable within the academic year.
J.4 Receiving a hardship bursary does not affect eligibility for J.1–J.3.

PART K — DATA PROTECTION
K.1 Information supplied is used only to assess student-finance applications and is deleted 6 years after the last payment.
K.2 Parental information supplied for independent students is deleted at the end of the assessment and is not used.
K.3 Applicants may request a copy of their data at any time from the Student Finance Office.

PART L — CHANGE LOG
2026-05-12  Part E thresholds raised by approx. 5 % for inflation. D.2 extended: work-study earnings now excluded for ALL students (previously dependent students only).
2025-05-20  B.3 added (registered civil partnerships).
2024-06-01  F.1 asset cap raised from EUR 30,000 to EUR 40,000.

A. ENTERPRISE LICENCE AGREEMENT TES-ELA-2023-118 (signed 1 March 2023) — EXTRACTS
======================================================================
1. Definitions
1.1 "Software" — Tessellate CAD Enterprise, including the desktop client, the web viewer and the rendering server components.
1.2 "Licence" — a named-user subscription licence to use the Software. One Licence permits one Named User to use the Software on any number of devices.
1.3 "Licensee Affiliates" — entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with the Licensee; their use counts as the Licensee's use.
1.4 "Named User" — an individual human being who is authorised by the Licensee to access the Software and has an active account on the Measurement Date. An individual is one Named User regardless of how many accounts the individual holds.
1.5 Shared accounts. Where an account is used by more than one individual, each individual who used that account during the three months ending on the Measurement Date is a Named User. The Licensee shall keep login records sufficient to identify such individuals.
1.6 Service accounts. An account used solely by software processes through the rendering-server API, without interactive login, is a "Service Account" and is not a Named User. If an individual logs in interactively through a Service Account at any time during the three months ending on the Measurement Date, that individual is a Named User.
1.7 "Active account" — any account that exists on the Measurement Date, unless it was disabled or deleted at least 30 days before the Measurement Date.
1.8 "Measurement Date" — 31 August of each year of the term.
1.9 "Production Environment" — any installation of the Software other than a registered Non-Production Environment (see Amendment No. 2).

2. Grant of licence and restrictions
2.1 Tessellate grants the Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the Software during the term for its internal business purposes, up to the number of Licences held.
2.2 The Licensee shall not (a) sublicense, rent or lease the Software; (b) use the Software to provide design services to third parties other than its own customers under contracts for vessels designed or built by the Licensee; (c) circumvent licence controls.
2.3 The Software may be installed in any country in which the Licensee or its Licensee Affiliates operate, subject to export control laws.
2.4 Plug-ins developed by the Licensee using the Tessellate SDK may be used without additional licences, but each individual using them requires a Licence as a Named User.

3. Use by third parties
3.1 The Licensee may permit its contractors and outsourcing providers to use the Software solely for the Licensee's internal business purposes.
3.2 Contractors and outsourcing providers who use the Software under 3.1 are Named Users of the Licensee and require Licences, unless the contractor uses the contractor's own Tessellate licences under the contractor's own agreement and the Licensee has received written confirmation of this from Tessellate.
3.3 The Licensee is responsible for the compliance of such third parties.

4. Fees
4.1 Subscription fees are invoiced annually in advance on 1 March for all Licences held.
4.2 Licences added during a subscription year are invoiced pro rata from their licence start date to the next 1 March.
4.3 List price for 2026: EUR 2,340 per Licence per year.

5. True-up
5.1 Each year the Licensee reports the number of Named Users as of the Measurement Date.
5.2 The number of Licences held on the Measurement Date is the number of Licences under all Order Forms whose licence start date is on or before the Measurement Date.
5.3 If the number of Named Users exceeds the number of Licences held, the Licensee purchases the shortfall at the then-current list price, with back-dated subscription fees for 12 months.
5.4 A true-up shortfall of more than 15 Licences, or of more than 10 % of Licences held, entitles Tessellate to conduct an audit at the Licensee's expense.

6. Audit
6.1 Tessellate may audit the Licensee's use of the Software once per year on 30 days' notice, in addition to any audit under 5.4.
6.2 The Licensee shall provide login records, identity management exports and Order Forms on request.
6.3 If an audit reveals a shortfall that the Licensee did not report in its True-Up Report, the Licensee pays the shortfall at 125 % of list price.

7. Term
7.1 The ELA runs until 28 February 2028 and may be renewed for further five-year terms.

8. Support and maintenance
8.1 Support is included in the subscription fee. Support cases may be raised by up to five designated contacts of the Licensee.
8.2 New releases are made available to all Licences held; the Licensee may continue to use the previous major release for 12 months after a new major release.

9. Data protection
9.1 Login records processed by Tessellate for licence management are processed as a processor on behalf of the Licensee; they are deleted 24 months after collection.

Post-incident severity review for INC-2026-0908-114 ("Invoice API elevated 5xx, eu-west")
Pack contents: (A) Incident Severity Runbook ISR, version 5.0, with Change Notice CN-5.1; (B) Security Incident Classification Standard SICS-2 (extract); (C) glossary extract from the Platform Handbook; (D) incident timeline and monitoring data; (E) customer impact data; (F) on-call notes.

======================================================================
(A) INCIDENT SEVERITY RUNBOOK ISR v5.0 (effective 1 February 2026)
======================================================================
1. Purpose
1.1 The severity of an incident determines paging, communication cadence, executive notification and the post-incident review format. The final severity is set at the post-incident review according to this runbook, based on the facts established after the incident; the severity declared during the incident is provisional.
1.2 This runbook covers availability, performance and data incidents. Security incidents (suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, data exfiltration, credential compromise) are classified under SICS-2 instead; where an incident is both, the higher of the two severities applies.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Active tenant" — a tenant that sent at least one API request in the 7 days before the incident started.
2.2 "Affected tenant" — an active tenant for which more than 5 % of its API requests failed (5xx or timeout) in at least one 10-minute monitoring window during the incident. Tenants with some failed requests below that rate in every window are not affected tenants.
2.3 "Enterprise tenant" — a tenant on an Enterprise plan with a signed Enterprise Master Services Agreement. Tenants on an Enterprise Trial (evaluation) plan are not Enterprise tenants for the purposes of this runbook.
2.4 "Payment processing" — the authorisation, capture, refund and payout APIs, and the ledger writes behind them. Invoicing, billing documents (invoice PDFs, statements), reporting and the merchant dashboard are not payment processing.
2.5 "Incident duration" — the time from the start of the first 10-minute monitoring window in which the incident's failure criterion was met to the end of the last such window. Alerting, acknowledgement and verification times are not part of the incident duration.
2.6 "Workaround" — a documented alternative that allows affected tenants to complete the affected operation without LatticePay intervention (e.g. a fallback endpoint), communicated to them on the status page or directly.
2.7 "Data loss" — loss of data that LatticePay had acknowledged as received. Data that can be restored automatically from the write-ahead log or replayed from the event archive, without manual reconstruction and with no more than 15 minutes of data affected, is "recoverable within RPO".

3. Base severity (impact)
3.1 SEV-1: more than 40 % of active tenants affected; or any unrecoverable data loss; or complete unavailability of payment processing in any region for 5 minutes or more.
3.2 SEV-2: more than 10 % and up to 40 % of active tenants affected; or 3 or more Enterprise tenants affected.
3.3 SEV-3: at least 1 % and up to 10 % of active tenants affected; or 1 or 2 Enterprise tenants affected.
3.4 SEV-4: fewer than 1 % of active tenants affected and no Enterprise tenant affected.
3.5 Where several criteria apply, the highest resulting severity is the base severity.

4. Adjustments (applied to the base severity in this order)
4.1 Duration: if the incident duration is more than 4 hours, raise the severity by one level (SEV-4 → SEV-3, SEV-3 → SEV-2, SEV-2 → SEV-1).
4.2 Workaround: if a Workaround was available to all affected tenants for the whole incident duration after the first 30 minutes, lower the severity by one level.
4.3 An adjustment never moves the severity above SEV-1 or below SEV-4.

5. Communication by severity
5.1 SEV-1: status page within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes; executive on-call paged; customer RCA within 5 business days.
5.2 SEV-2: status page within 30 minutes; updates hourly; customer RCA within 10 business days.
5.3 SEV-3: status page if more than 20 tenants affected; internal review only.
5.4 SEV-4: no status page; ticket-level follow-up.

6. Roles
6.1 Incident commander (IC): declares provisional severity, coordinates responders.
6.2 Communications lead: status page and Enterprise account managers.
6.3 Scribe: timeline in the incident channel.
6.4 Service owner: confirms the technical facts used for the final severity (affected tenants, duration, data impact) in writing before the review.
6.5 The IC's provisional severity is not changed during the incident for reclassification purposes; reclassification happens only at the review.

7. Post-incident review
7.1 A post-incident review is held within 5 business days for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and within 15 business days for SEV-3. SEV-4 incidents are reviewed in the weekly operations meeting.
7.2 The review records the final severity, the facts on which it is based and the corrective actions.
7.3 Final severity drives the reliability scorecard: SEV-1 = 10 points, SEV-2 = 5, SEV-3 = 2, SEV-4 = 0.

8. Historical note
8.1 ISR v4.2 (in force until 31 January 2026) used "tenants with any failed request" as affected tenants and treated Enterprise Trial tenants as Enterprise tenants. It had no workaround adjustment and no floors.

Appendix — Recent final severities (for consistency checks)
INC-2026-0114-021 | ISR v4.2 | 212 of 3,870 tenants with any failure (5.5 %) | 1 Enterprise | SEV-3
INC-2026-0322-067 | ISR v5.0 | 44 affected of 3,950 (1.1 %) | 0 Enterprise | 2 h 10 min | Workaround from 00:12 | SEV-4
INC-2026-0611-088 | ISR v5.0 + CN-5.1 | Payouts API degraded 22 min, 0.8 % affected | SEV-2 (payment processing floor)
INC-2026-0729-102 | ISR v5.0 + CN-5.1 | 9.4 % affected | 1 Enterprise | 4 h 30 min | SEV-2 (duration raise)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CHANGE NOTICE CN-5.1 (approved by the Reliability Council, effective 1 June 2026)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
CN-5.1.1 New section 4.4: "Floor for Enterprise impact. After the adjustments in 4.1 and 4.2, an incident in which at least one Enterprise tenant was affected is never below SEV-3."
CN-5.1.2 New section 3.6: "Payment processing floor. Any incident in which payment processing was degraded (more than 5 % failed requests in a 10-minute window) for 15 minutes or more is at least SEV-2 before adjustments."
CN-5.1.3 Section 2.7 is amended by adding: "Data that is recoverable only by manual reconstruction, or where more than 15 minutes of data is affected, is recoverable but not within RPO; such an incident is at least SEV-2 before adjustments."

======================================================================
(B) SECURITY INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION STANDARD SICS-2 — EXTRACT
======================================================================
S1 Any confirmed unauthorised access to cardholder data: S-1 (maps to SEV-1).
S2 Suspected unauthorised access under investigation: S-2 (maps to SEV-2) until closed.
S3 Vulnerability discovered without evidence of exploitation: S-3 (maps to SEV-3).
S4 A security review opened as routine follow-up to an availability incident, where no unauthorised access is suspected, is not a security incident.

======================================================================
(C) PLATFORM HANDBOOK — GLOSSARY EXTRACT
======================================================================
Invoice API — generates invoice documents (PDF/UBL) for merchants' customers and stores them in the document store. Part of the Billing Documents product.
Payments API — authorisation, capture, refund; Payouts API — merchant settlements.
Webhook dispatcher — delivers event notifications to tenants; events are persisted in the event archive for 30 days and can be replayed automatically.
Regions: eu-west (primary for EU tenants), eu-central (DR).

======================================================================
(D) INCIDENT TIMELINE (UTC) AND MONITORING
======================================================================
8 September 2026
13:31 Deployment of document-store client library 4.12.0 to Invoice API pods in eu-west.
13:40–13:50 First 10-minute monitoring window in which the Invoice API 5xx rate exceeded 5 % for affected tenants.
13:41 Alert "invoice-api 5xx > 2 %" fired; on-call acknowledged 13:44.
13:52 IC declared provisional SEV-2 ("wide customer impact, cause unknown, payments?").
14:05 Payments API, Payouts API: error rates checked — normal (0.02 %); no degradation of authorisation, capture or refund at any time during the incident.
14:08 Workaround published on the status page and sent to all tenants with failed requests: "Use the v1 invoice endpoint /v1/invoices/render (synchronous) until further notice." The v1 endpoint remained fully available throughout.
14:47 Webhook dispatcher backlog; 11 minutes of "invoice.rendered" events (14:36–14:47) dropped from the in-memory queue during a pod restart.
15:10 Event replay from the event archive started automatically for 14:36–14:47; completed 15:18; no manual steps.
16:55 Rollback to library 4.11.3 started.
17:30–17:40 Last 10-minute monitoring window with 5xx rate above 5 %.
17:51 IC declared all-clear after verification.
Security: on 9 September a routine security review ticket SEC-REV-2231 was opened "as standard follow-up to any library-related incident"; no unauthorised access suspected; closed 11 September with no findings.

======================================================================
(E) CUSTOMER IMPACT DATA (analytics export, 10 September 2026)
======================================================================
Active tenants (at least one request in the 7 days before 13:31 on 8 September): 4,020. Provisioned tenants (all, including dormant): 5,610.
Tenants with at least one failed Invoice API request during the incident: 455.
Tenants with more than 5 % of API requests failed in at least one 10-minute window: 318.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 318:
  T-10044 Moravia Retail Group — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed 2023.
  T-11820 Kestrel Hospitality — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed March 2026.
  T-12977 Orinoco Sports GmbH — Enterprise Trial plan (evaluation until 30 September 2026); MSA under negotiation.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 137 tenants with failures below 5 % in every window: T-10390 Harwell Foods (Enterprise, MSA 2024).
Payments API volume during the incident: normal; no tenant had payment failures above baseline.

======================================================================
(F) ON-CALL NOTES
======================================================================
IC handover note (18:05): "Total impact roughly 4 h 10 min from first alert to all-clear. Three Enterprise customers affected, 455 tenants saw errors. Webhook events lost for 11 min but replayed. Suggest keeping SEV-2 for the review."
Communications lead: status page updates posted 14:02, 14:08, 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 17:55. Account managers of T-10044, T-11820 and T-12977 informed.
Root-cause summary (engineering, 10 September): "Library 4.12.0 changed the default connection-pool size for the document store from 64 to 8. Under normal afternoon load, render requests queued and timed out after 30 s, returning 504. The synchronous v1 endpoint uses a separate pool and was unaffected. The in-memory webhook queue lost events on the pod restart at 14:47 because the graceful-shutdown hook was also affected; the archive-based replay worked as designed."
Corrective actions proposed: pin pool size in configuration; canary deployments for library upgrades; alert threshold review.

Section 2 assigns exception levels: 0 means no operative exception; 1 means requested but unauthorized; 2 means authorized but unused; 3 means used for a shipment. Section 4 says an authorization may be withdrawn until the warehouse first relies on it by bypassing validation or releasing the parcel. Section 7 says packing notes are evidentiary only: copying an authorization does not itself constitute reliance, and a note copied after withdrawal does not restore authority. A portal address correction processed normally is not use of an exception.

The parcel remains in the cage. A shift summary calls the order “authorized for override,” but it was generated from packing-note text rather than the authority register.
